title: Incident Bot v2: Slack interactive actions ack/retry + idempotency + degraded-mode UX
creator: Miles Thornton
description:
Context
Slack interactive components (buttons, select menus, modal submits) require an acknowledgement within ~3 seconds. During incidents, our bot frequently makes upstream calls (deploy metadata, config diffs, telemetry aggregations). When those calls are slow or timing out, we currently miss Slack ack deadlines, causing:
- User-facing “Something went wrong” / actions that appear to do nothing
- Duplicate clicks/retries in the channel that amplify load (especially during Sev0/Sev1)
- Non-deterministic state in threads (multiple cards posted, partial updates)

This ticket hardens Slack interactions for Incident Bot v2 by implementing:
1) Fast ack + async completion patterns
2) Retry handling with explicit idempotency
3) Graceful degradation when upstream queries time out / are rate limited
4) Better operator messaging and “fallback to links” behavior when live context can’t be fetched

Problem statement
We need Slack actions to be dependable under stress: ack quickly, complete work asynchronously, remain safe under Slack retries, and avoid multiplying load when core dependencies are unhealthy.

Goals / Non-goals
Goals
- 99% of interactive actions ack within 1s (p50 < 200ms) even when upstream dependencies are slow.
- Slack retries do not create duplicate side effects (duplicate cards, repeated telemetry fanout, repeated modal opens).
- Consistent degraded-mode UX: cached context + deep links + “manual fallback commands” snippet.
- Clear errors: distinguish “permission denied” vs “timeout” vs “rate limited” vs “partial results.”

Non-goals
- Re-architect bot backend. Keep changes scoped to interaction handler + shared request wrapper.
- Replace telemetry query service caching/rate limiting (covered by ENG-5427 / ENG-5429).

Requirements
A. Ack + async completion
- For all interactive payloads (block_actions, view_submission, shortcuts):
  - Immediately ack with an ephemeral “Working…” message OR a modal “Loading…” state.
  - Perform upstream queries asynchronously.
  - Update the original message/modal when results are ready.
- Time budget targets:
  - Ack path: no external network calls; only local validation + enqueue.
  - Async completion: soft timeout 6s per dependency; hard timeout 12s overall before degraded-mode.

B. Retry + idempotency
- Use Slack retry headers (X-Slack-Retry-Num / X-Slack-Retry-Reason) to detect retries.
- Implement idempotency keys per interaction event:
  - Base key: team_id + channel_id + message_ts (or view_id) + action_id + slack_trigger_id + user_id
  - Store in Redis with TTL 10 minutes.
  - If key exists, do not re-run upstream queries; return existing result state (or “already in progress”).
- Ensure idempotency covers side effects:
  - Posting/updating cards
  - Opening modals
  - Expanding config diffs / pagination

C. Failure modes and degraded behavior
- If any upstream dependency times out / circuit breaker open / rate limited:
  - Return partial results if available.
  - Otherwise show degraded-mode card section:
    - “Live diagnostics currently unavailable”
    - Link buttons to relevant Console dashboards and SLO burn views (pre-parameterized time window)
    - Provide 1–2 manual fallback commands (e.g., internal slash command equivalents) when appropriate
    - Include correlation ids / request ids for debugging
- If action requires privileged scope and the caller lacks permission:
  - Do not degrade silently. Show explicit “Insufficient permission” with guidance:
    - “Request access” link or “break-glass during Sev0/Sev1” pointer (no secrets in Slack)

D. Observability
- Add metrics and logs:
  - slack_interaction_ack_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99)
  - slack_interaction_async_duration_ms
  - slack_interaction_retry_count
  - slack_interaction_idempotency_hit_rate
  - slack_interaction_degraded_mode_rate (by reason: timeout, rate_limited, circuit_open, unknown)
- Ensure logs include: interaction_type, action_id, correlation_id, retry_num, idempotency_key_hash (not raw key).

E. Test coverage
- Unit tests for:
  - idempotency key derivation + TTL behavior
  - retry detection
  - ack path does not call upstream clients
- E2E tests in incidents channel harness:
  - simulate delayed telemetry endpoint -> bot still acks and later updates
  - simulate Slack retry event -> no duplicate card
  - simulate timeout -> degraded-mode payload renders correctly

Proposed implementation sketch
- Introduce InteractionJobQueue (lightweight): enqueue work item on ack path.
- Create InteractionState store (Redis):
  - states: in_progress, complete, failed_degraded
  - store minimal response payload for replays (e.g., message update blocks JSON as string)
- Wrap upstream calls with shared helper:
  - budgeted timeouts + cancellation
  - propagate typed error (timeout/rate_limit/permission)
- Slack UX:
  - Buttons should transition to disabled state (where possible) when in_progress.
  - For modal submits: ack immediately, then update modal contents (or push a follow-up ephemeral message) with result/degraded.

Acceptance criteria
- Interactive actions in #incidents and #eng-oncall ack within 1s at p99 in staging load test.
- Slack retry simulation does not generate duplicate thread cards or duplicate telemetry queries.
- When telemetry query service is slow/unhealthy, bot surfaces degraded-mode links within 5–10s with a clear reason.
- Metrics dashboard exists and can be used during beta to monitor ack latency + degraded rate.

Links / References
- Related tickets:
  - ENG-5427 Telemetry query service cache + coalescing
  - ENG-5429 Diagnostics load shedding
- Related PRs (tracking):
  - incident-bot PR-1854 (modal pagination + caching) (baseline)
  - incident-bot PR-1862 (E2E tests for #incidents) (will validate this ticket)
  - incident-bot PR-1865 (timeout handling improvements) (align error messaging)
- Slack platform notes:
  - Must ack interactive events quickly; retries are expected under latency.

Rollout plan
- Ship behind incident-bot-v2-interactions-hardening feature flag.
- Enable for SRE beta cohort only (per ENG-5428).
- Monitor:
  - ack p99
  - degraded-mode rate
  - retry count
  - error logs spike
- If degraded-mode rate > 20% for 30 minutes during active incidents, auto-fallback to “links-only” mode (ties into ENG-5429).
comments: 2025-02-14 (Devon Price): Drafted idempotency key format and Redis schema. Planning to hash key before logging to avoid leaking channel/user identifiers into logs. Ack path will only validate signature + parse payload + enqueue job.

2025-02-18 (Logan Wright): Please ensure async completion respects telemetry query budgets. If bot retries cause additional fanout we’ll see query latency spikes again. Recommend explicit “already in progress” response on duplicate actions rather than re-enqueueing.

2025-02-20 (Aisha Bello): Add a counter for degraded-mode by reason; we need to distinguish timeouts vs rate-limit vs circuit-open for alert tuning. Also please tag metrics by action_id so we can identify noisy interactions.

2025-02-24 (Miles Thornton): Confirmed Slack retries observed in prod during Feb 7th regression incident. Duplicate button clicks created ~5x telemetry load and multiple “Recent deploys” cards. This ticket is a blocker for broad rollout.

2025-02-28 (Devon Price): Implemented ack+enqueue for block_actions and view_submission. Added idempotency check with 10m TTL. Added typed errors for timeout/rate_limit/permission and a degraded-mode renderer that includes Console links + manual commands. Opening PR in incident-bot this afternoon.

2025-03-04 (Dylan Brooks): Review feedback: ensure modal updates are idempotent too (use view_id). Also disable buttons while in_progress to reduce repeat clicks. Please add a single “Request ID” field to degraded-mode so we can correlate logs quickly.

2025-03-06 (Devon Price): Addressed feedback; added view_id-based keys, disabled-state on buttons where supported, and request_id surfacing. E2E tests in progress; will rely on PR-1862 harness for retry simulation. Marking In Review pending CI + SRE signoff.
